question: Can wait-duration features with a class-balanced, CV-tuned gradient-boosting model predict whether one extra unit of resource capacity reduces makespan better than a random forest on count-only wait features?
method: Simulated single-resource scheduling instances (numpy); serial schedule-generation at capacity C and C+1; label = makespan drops. Stratified 70/30 split, fixed seed.

dataset.name: Simulated single-cumulative-resource scheduling instances (numpy, generated at run time)

baseline: Random forest (300 trees) on count-only wait features: instance size, capacity, and sorted per-task counts of resource releases waited through.
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM with hyper-parameters chosen by cross-validation on the training set, using the same counts plus total, mean, and maximum wait durations.
notes: Labels come from a simple serial SGS heuristic on random instances, not from the paper's CP solver search; results describe this simulation only. The paper's reported result is not stated. Test set used once; tuning used training-set CV only. Both models use the same seeds (42, 43, 44) and the same evaluation function.
